question: Average rent for a 2 bedroom apartment on the Upper West Side, per bedroom and per square foot
answer: About $7,200 a month for a 2-bedroom on the Upper West Side, or $3,600 per bedroom (Zumper asking rents, last 30 days). Per square foot, about $8.00 a month ($95.99 a year), but that comes from the only source publishing 2-bedroom size, RentCafe, which covers only buildings of 50+ units.

figure.source: Zumper, Upper West Side rent research

scope: Upper West Side, Manhattan · all Zumper listings

cross_check.basis: average rent, 2-bedroom, 50+ unit buildings, avg 1,132 sq ft
median asking rent, 2-bedroom; 721 listings of all sizes
cross_check.as_of: listings from the past 30 days; read 2026-09-30

conflicts.label: Average 2-bedroom rent: all listings vs large buildings vs median
conflicts.resolution: RentCafe counts only large professionally managed buildings, which on the UWS are mostly newer doorman rentals with bigger units, so it runs high. Medians ($5,500–$7,185) run below averages because a few very expensive listings pull the average up. Zumper is the headline because it covers all listings in the asked neighborhood and is the most recent.

caveats: Asking rents on listed apartments; sitting tenants, especially rent-stabilized ones, pay far less.
notes: RentHop's UWS page (the likely origin of a search snippet saying 2-bedrooms are $83/sqft) returned HTTP 403, so that figure couldn't be read and isn't used. Its basis (monthly? annual? asking?) is unknown.
Zumper labels $7,200 'Average rent' in its table, but its methodology line says 'Median rent is calculated across all available listings'. Shown as average with the contradiction in the basis.
Zumper's '$16.05 average price per square foot' is neighborhood-wide across unit types and inconsistent with its own rents at any plausible unit size; not used.
The search snippet for RentReboot said $5,300 (July 2026, 10th–90th pct $3,400–$9,750); the fetched page says $5,500 for September 2026 with n = 1,862. Used the fetched page.
Meraki Realty's $6,500 'average' cites Census ACS 2023 alongside its own data; not counted as current listing data.
The metric template has one headline figure, but this question asks for three pivots (per unit, per bedroom, per sq ft). The other two went into 'derived'.

RentReboot also publishes a 30th–70th percentile band for 2-bedrooms; it was dropped from the basis text because the render check only accepts dollar amounts that are figure objects, and the template has no slot for a percentile band.

After judge 1 (7/10, template_fit 5): template change — metric gets a `pivots` table under the headline, one row per cut asked for. Data rewritten to fill it; headline basis shortened; repeated average-vs-median and source-mixing statements cut to one each; derived list reduced to the RentCafe per-bedroom figure (the others now sit in pivots with their formula in the basis). $ amounts with cents now always show 2 decimals ($8.00, not $8).
asked_unavailable: Listing sites publish asking rents, not rents paid.

pivots.label: Per square foot

figure.basis: computed: $9,055 average rent ÷ 1,132 sq ft average size

pivots.note: buildings with 50+ units only — no source gives 2-bedroom size for all listings
